jobs.title: 1234-Medical Coding Specialist
jobs.description:
About the Role

The Medical Coding Specialist is responsible for independently reviewing, analyzing, and resolving all assigned front-end scrubs and denied claims to ensure accurate and timely claim payment. This position focuses on identifying and correcting coding-related issues prior to claim submission, resubmitting corrected claims or appealing denied claims, applying established coding guidelines, payer requirements, and organizational policies. The Coding Specialist works closely with revenue cycle partners to prevent claim rejections, support clean claim rates, and promote efficient reimbursement processes. This role requires strong attention to detail, foundational coding knowledge, and the ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment.

A Day in the Life

  • Averages 10 front-end holds/denials per hour
  • Reviews coding and resubmits corrected claims to insurance
  • Creates  appeal letters/forms with medical documentation
  • Maintains a minimum of 92% coding accuracy.
  • Assigns ICD-10-CM and CPT codes with appropriate modifiers for services provided in the professional fee environment.
  • Reviews medical records and all applicable documentation to determine appropriate codes for documented services and diagnoses.
  • Ensures all diagnosis codes meet local and national medical necessity guidelines.
  • Utilizes internal coding resources, payer guidelines, and other reference materials to ensure accurate and compliant coding for all assigned services.
  • Follows all HIPAA regulations and upholds the highest standards of privacy and confidentiality.
  • Maintains current knowledge of laws, regulations, payer policies, and industry guidance impacting compliant coding practices.
  • Independently reviews and resolves all assigned front-end claim holds.
  • Actively participates in department meetings, one-on-one meetings, and mentorship meetings with the assigned Coding Team Lead.
  • Escalates identified client trends to the assigned Coding Manager.
  • Escalates all coding-related questions to the assigned Coding manager for guidance and clarification.
  • Maintains and completes all CEU requirements.
  • Performs other duties or tasks as assigned

 What You Need

  • Must hold a current AAPC or AHIMA Coding Certification for a minimum of 3 years.
  • Minimum of 3+ years of professional coding experience.
  • Strong working knowledge of CPT, ICD-10-CM, medical terminology, anatomy and physiology, and state and federal Medicare reimbursement guidelines.
  • Prior experience in reviewing front end coding errors before submitting to insurance
  • Prior experience in reviewing and correcting coding from insurance denials. 
  • Prior experience in submitting corrected claims and appeals.
  • Prior experience with insurance guidelines and EOBs.
  • Familiarity with proper English grammar, usage, and professional documentation standards.
  • Ability to research and analyze data, draw logical conclusions, and resolve coding or documentation issues.
  • Ability to read, interpret, and apply policies, procedures, laws, and regulations.
  • Ability to accurately read and interpret medical documentation, clinical terminology, and documented procedures.
  • Demonstrated ability to exercise independent judgment in coding and claim resolution.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare reports, clarify documentation needs, and maintain collaborative working relationships with physicians and staff.
  • Strong commitment to maintaining confidentiality and safeguarding protected health information.
  • Prior experience working in a medical billing environment with strict adherence to HIPAA compliance requirements.
  • Demonstrated proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams).

We offer competitive benefits to set you up for success in and outside of work.

Here’s What We Offer

jobs.description:
About the Role


This is a senior, high-visibility role at the intersection of Sales, Product, and Customer Success — one that carries real influence over how Innovaccer enters and wins in two of its most strategically important market segments. The Payer and Public Sector markets are growth priorities for the company, and the right candidate will have the opportunity to shape segment strategy, earn credibility with C-suite buyers, and drive meaningful impact on pipeline and product direction from day one.

You will be the primary subject matter expert and strategic advisor for the Payer and Public Sector segments, working across enterprise deals of all sizes and stages. You collaborate closely with Sales leadership, Product, and Customer Success, and serve as a thought leader both internally and externally 

A Day in the Life

Segment Strategy & Market Leadership

  • Define and continuously refine the go-to-market strategy for the Payer and Public Sector segments, including market prioritization, competitive positioning, and solution packaging.
  • Translate deep domain knowledge of payer operations, Medicaid managed care, Medicare Advantage, and government health programs into actionable strategy and compelling narratives for prospects and internal stakeholders.
  • Identify white space, emerging policy trends, and shifts in the competitive landscape that inform both near-term pipeline activity and longer-term product investment.

Deal Support & Executive Engagement

jobs.title: 4211-Director-Platform Marketing
jobs.description:
About the Role

We at Innovaccer are looking for a Director, Platform Marketing to build and lead the marketing function for Gravity — our AI-native platform that makes autonomous healthcare operations possible. This is the most senior marketing role in the Gravity organization. You set the strategy, build the team, own the platform narrative, and are ultimately accountable for the pipeline all of Gravity's swimlanes produce.

Where each solution's Head of Marketing owns a specific buyer and a specific outcome, you own the layer underneath all of them. You own how Innovaccer explains the platform — Memory, Intelligence, and Orchestrated Execution — and why that architecture is what makes autonomous operations credible and differentiated. You build the team of marketers who execute each swimlane, and you hold each of them to the same pipeline standard the solution Heads of Marketing are held to.

This is a player-coach role at the outset: you will set the strategy and build the team while also executing directly in the early innings, particularly on the platform narrative and analyst relationships. As the team scales, the balance shifts toward leadership and organizational design. You report to the CMO.

A Day in the Life

  • Define and own the overall Gravity marketing strategy — how the platform is positioned, which swimlanes are prioritized and when, and how the Gravity story nests inside Innovaccer's broader autonomous operations narrative.
  • Set and hold accountability for the aggregate pipeline target across all Gravity swimlanes. Each swimlane has its own pipeline number; you own the sum.
  • Build, hire, and lead the Gravity marketing team — including swimlane marketers, a platform narrative function, and technical/analyst-facing content. This is a team you are building, not inheriting fully formed.
  • Own the platform narrative for Gravity — how Memory, Intelligence, and Orchestrated Execution work together to make autonomous operations reliable — and keep it current as the architecture evolves.
  • Lead analyst relations at the platform level — briefing KLAS, Gartner, Forrester, and relevant technical analysts on Gravity's architecture and differentiation, distinct from any single solution's analyst conversations.
  • Partner directly with the CMO, the CEO, and Gravity's Product and Engineering leadership to ensure the platform story is technically accurate, commercially relevant, and updated as capabilities ship.
  • Work with technology partners (e.g., NVIDIA) on joint technical narrative and co-marketing tied to platform-level capability, not individual solutions.
  • Coordinate with each solution's Head of Marketing so their pitches draw on a consistent, credible platform story rather than each team explaining Gravity differently.
  • Represent Gravity externally — at analyst briefings, industry events, and with technical evaluators inside prospective customers who are assessing whether the architecture can deliver what solution teams are claiming.
  • Track competitive positioning across AI and healthcare data infrastructure platforms and flag where Gravity's differentiation needs to be sharpened or better articulated.
  • Build the library of reusable technical proof points — architecture diagrams, benchmark data, security and governance documentation — that every solution team, the Head of Thought Leadership, and the sales organization can draw on.

What You Need

  • Either of two backgrounds: (a) 8–10 years in management consulting or strategy, ideally followed by an MBA from a top-tier program, with meaningful exposure to healthcare and a demonstrated track record of owning go-to-market outcomes, not just producing strategy recommendations; or (b) 10–14 years in marketing at an AI, AI-infrastructure, or healthcare technology company, with direct experience leading a marketing function, owning pipeline, and building team. Either path is a fit — we are not requiring both.
  • A proven track record of owning a pipeline or commercial outcome at the function level — not as a contributor to someone else's number. For path (a), this includes consulting engagements tied to a client's measurable commercial result. For path (b), owning and delivering marketing pipeline directly. This is a hard requirement for both paths.
  • Experience building and leading marketing teams, including hiring, structuring a function, and developing talent. This is a people leadership role from day one.
  • Genuine comfort with technical material — you need to understand enough of how an AI platform is architected (data, models, orchestration, governance) to translate it accurately for both technical evaluators and business buyers, and to hold your team accountable for doing the same.
  • Experience with analyst relations at a senior level — briefing Gartner, Forrester, KLAS, or equivalent analysts on platform architecture and differentiation, not just product features.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to make complex technical concepts credible and clear for both engineering-minded evaluators and C-suite buyers.
  • Comfort operating cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, and Sales leadership at a peer level — this role has significant organizational influence and no formal authority over most of the people it depends on.
  • Healthcare industry experience is a strong plus — direct healthcare AI experience is ideal, but genuine demonstrated fluency in the healthcare buyer environment is the floor.
  • Comfort building in ambiguity — this function is still being defined. The Director, Platform Marketing is not stepping into a mature org; they are building it.

We offer competitive benefits to set you up for success in and outside of work.

Here’s What We Offer

  • Generous Paid Time Off: Recharge and relax with 20 days of fixed time off per year, in addition to company holidays—because we believe work-life balance fuels performance.
  • Best-in-Class Parental Leave: Spend quality time with your growing family. We offer one of the industry’s most generous parental leave policies to support you during life’s most important moments.
